claim: Buck converter maximum duty cycle is calculated as D = VOUT / (VIN(max) x eta), with efficiency typically estimated at 90% for worst-case sizing.
stance_target: buck converter design methodology for ECE power electronics projects
scope_conditions: integrated-switch buck converter IC operating in continuous conduction mode
quoted_support: Use either an estimated factor, e.g., 90% (which is not unrealistic for a buck converter worst-case efficiency), or see the Typical Characteristics section of the data sheet of the selected converter.

claim: Inductor ripple current for a buck converter should be estimated as 20% to 40% of the maximum output current when no data sheet range is given.
quoted_support: A good estimation for the inductor ripple current is 20% to 40% of the output current.

claim: Feedback divider current must be at least 100 times the feedback bias current to keep output-voltage-setting error under 1%.
stance_target: output voltage setting resistor divider design
scope_conditions: resistive divider output voltage setting for buck converter ICs
quoted_support: The current through the resistive divider needs to be at least 100 times as big as the feedback bias current... This adds less than 1% inaccuracy to the voltage measurement.

claim: Schottky rectifier diode average forward current in a buck converter equals IOUT(max) x (1-D).
stance_target: rectifier diode selection for buck converters
